cards.back: Breaking food down into tiny pieces that your body can absorb and use.
cards.say: digestion. Breaking food down into tiny pieces that your body can absorb and use.

cards.back: Where digestion begins. Teeth break food into small pieces and saliva makes it wet.
cards.say: mouth. Where digestion begins. Teeth break food into small pieces and saliva makes it wet.

cards.back: Sharp, flat front teeth that cut and bite food.
cards.say: incisors. Sharp, flat front teeth that cut and bite food.

cards.back: Pointed teeth that tear food.
cards.say: canines. Pointed teeth that tear food.

cards.back: Wide, flat back teeth that crush and grind food.
cards.say: molars. Wide, flat back teeth that crush and grind food.

cards.back: A liquid made in the mouth. It wets food and starts to break down starch.
cards.say: saliva. A liquid made in the mouth. It wets food and starts to break down starch.

cards.back: The tube, also called the gullet, that carries food from the mouth to the stomach.
cards.say: oesophagus. The tube, also called the gullet, that carries food from the mouth to the stomach.

cards.back: Waves of muscle squeezing that push food along the gut.
cards.say: peristalsis. Waves of muscle squeezing that push food along the gut.

cards.back: A stretchy bag where muscles churn food with acid and digestive juices.
cards.say: stomach. A stretchy bag where muscles churn food with acid and digestive juices.

cards.front: Why does the stomach contain acid?
cards.back: The acid helps to break down food and kills many harmful bacteria.
cards.say: Why does the stomach contain acid? The acid helps to break down food and kills many harmful bacteria.

cards.back: A long, coiled tube where digestion is finished and nutrients pass into the blood.
cards.say: small intestine. A long, coiled tube where digestion is finished and nutrients pass into the blood.

cards.back: Tiny finger-like parts lining the small intestine. They give a large surface for absorbing nutrients.
cards.say: villi. Tiny finger-like parts lining the small intestine. They give a large surface for absorbing nutrients.

cards.back: When digested nutrients pass through the wall of the small intestine into the blood.
cards.say: absorption. When digested nutrients pass through the wall of the small intestine into the blood.

cards.back: The tube after the small intestine. It absorbs water from the food that is left.
cards.say: large intestine. The tube after the small intestine. It absorbs water from the food that is left.

cards.back: The end of the gut where faeces are stored until you go to the toilet.
cards.say: rectum. The end of the gut where faeces are stored until you go to the toilet.

cards.back: The opening where faeces leave the body.
cards.say: anus. The opening where faeces leave the body.

cards.back: Waste left over after digestion, made of undigested food, fibre and water.
cards.say: faeces. Waste left over after digestion, made of undigested food, fibre and water.

cards.back: A large organ that makes bile. It also processes nutrients and removes harmful substances from the blood.
cards.say: liver. A large organ that makes bile. It also processes nutrients and removes harmful substances from the blood.

cards.back: A liquid made by the liver that helps to break up fats.
cards.say: bile. A liquid made by the liver that helps to break up fats.

cards.back: An organ that makes digestive juices that go into the small intestine.
cards.say: pancreas. An organ that makes digestive juices that go into the small intestine.

cards.back: A chemical that speeds up the breakdown of food. Saliva contains an enzyme.
cards.say: enzyme. A chemical that speeds up the breakdown of food. Saliva contains an enzyme.

cards.front: Put the main organs of the gut in order.
cards.back: Mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, anus.
cards.say: Put the main organs of the gut in order.. Mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, anus.

cards.front: Why do we chew our food?
cards.back: Smaller pieces have more surface for digestive juices to work on, and are easier to swallow.
cards.say: Why do we chew our food? Smaller pieces have more surface for digestive juices to work on, and are easier to swallow.

cards.front: Why do we need fibre in our food?
cards.back: Fibre cannot be digested, but it helps keep food moving through the gut.
cards.say: Why do we need fibre in our food? Fibre cannot be digested, but it helps keep food moving through the gut.
